venue.name: Beacon Hill Park
venue.description: Beacon Hill Park is a roughly 740,000 square metre City of Victoria park at 100 Cook Street that has belonged to the city since 1882 and contains natural areas, manicured flower beds, lakes, footpaths, sports fields and play equipment. Listed amenities include washrooms, a picnic shelter, play equipment, trails and paths, beach access and a Garry oak natural area, and the park also contains the separately operated Beacon Hill Children's Farm petting zoo and the Mile "0" marker of the Trans-Canada Highway.

programs.name: Self-guided park visit
programs.description: Beacon Hill Park is a public City of Victoria park that is open to visitors without booking. Listed amenities include washrooms, a picnic shelter, play equipment, sports fields, a ball diamond, trails and paths, beach access, a natural area and "Accessible Features". Within the park, dogs must be on-leash at all times except in the leash-optional area south of Dallas Road. The park also contains the separately operated Beacon Hill Children's Farm. No admission price, opening hours or group booking process for an ordinary self-guided visit is stated on the City page.
programs.evidence: Meandering footpaths offer long strolls among manicured and natural areas and features for the whole family to enjoy.

programs.name: Beacon Hill Park activity or event permit
programs.description: An organized activity or special event in Beacon Hill Park requires a permit. All proposed activities and events are assessed against an Appropriate Activity Assessment Framework by Parks Division staff, and Council approval may be necessary. Applications for smaller scale activities (fewer than 50 people) may be submitted two months before the date; larger events should be submitted at least four months ahead, so 60 days is recorded as the minimum lead time for a small group. The applicant must provide proof of public liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 naming the City of Victoria as additional insured. Permit fees and/or deposits apply but the amounts are not given in this document ("Please see application for current fees"). Alcohol is prohibited in the park, food sales are not permitted in Beacon Hill Park, and Island Health must be contacted if food or beverages are offered on site. Questions go to the Permit Clerk, Arts, Culture & Events, 720 Douglas Street. Document is dated November 2022.
programs.evidence: Smaller scale applications (less than 50 people) may be submitted two months prior to the proposed activity or event.

images.alt: A bird's eye view of Beacon Hill Park. Lush trees and green grass surround a peaceful pond.

gaps: The website listed in the directory, www.beaconhillpark.com, is NOT the park's own site. It is an unofficial promotional/history site built by a Victoria advertising agency, copyright 2001, with only Location, History, Photo Gallery and Links pages and no visitor, booking or accessibility information. Beacon Hill Park is owned and operated by the City of Victoria, so victoria.ca was used as the venue's own domain.
Admission is not stated anywhere. The park is a public city park but no page says it is free, so general admission and is_free are left null.
Opening hours for the park are not stated on the City page. hours_notes is null.
Washrooms and a picnic shelter appear only as one-word items in the City page's Amenities list; their locations, opening seasons and whether the picnic shelter can be reserved are not stated.
The Amenities list includes "Accessible Features" but does not say what they are, so wheelchair_accessible and stroller_accessible are left null.
Bus or coach parking, and school bus drop-off points, are not mentioned.
No education, school or interpretive programming for children's groups is advertised by the City for this park, and there is no named school-programs contact.
Permit fees and deposits are said to apply to activity/event permits but no dollar amount is published in the applicant information document; the amount is only "see application for current fees".
The applicant information PDF is dated November 2022 and may be out of date; the Park Permit Application form it refers to is a 2016 PDF.
It is not stated whether an ordinary daycare or class walking visit needs a permit at all, or only organized activities and special events.

Images: the City page's Open Graph image is a generic City of Victoria social card (sites/default/files/social/social.png) rather than a photo of the park, so the lead photo on the Beacon Hill Park page was recorded as the hero instead. That lead photo is the only photograph on the page, so neither program has an image of its own and both image_url values are null. No image credit or image reuse statement appears on the park page; the footer copyright line was recorded as rights_note. No photographs were taken from beaconhillpark.com, which is not the venue's own domain.
